details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:84-87 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `_trusted` treats any GitHub login ending in `[bot]` as trusted, allowing an external bot to plant an operator-step issue that the script adopts.
  WHY: `find_issue` can select and subsequently update an attacker-controlled issue without verifying the bot's repository association.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:123; scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:576-577 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Activation skip checks accept untrusted substring matches for activation markers instead of validating the complete marker and its author.
  WHY: A user-controlled linked issue body or tracking-issue comment can forge a marker and suppress legitimate verification.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:595-603 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `run_project_activation_verify` does not pass `TRACKING_NUM` to the project-mode subprocess.
  WHY: `activation_verify.sh` requires a numeric `TRACKING_NUM` and skips when it is unset; severity disagreement: one reviewer rated this MAJOR, while the others rated it BLOCKER.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:339 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The assignment-prefix regex recognizes `NAME=` but not `NAME+=`, so assignment-prefixed `git push` commands can evade the merged-PR push guard.
  WHY: The root hook diverges from its template and fails the `+=` guard tests; severity disagreement: reviewers described the CI impact as failing tests or a lint-gate failure, while rating the finding BLOCKER.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:134-138 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `render_body` can truncate the body at an arbitrary position, splitting an operator-step marker or entry content.
  WHY: Subsequent parsing may miss the truncated entry and leave orphaned text or append a duplicate.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:170 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `write_codex_config.sh` is called without explicit catalog and project paths.
  WHY: In consumer workflows, defaults can resolve against the consumer checkout rather than the support checkout, omitting the model catalog and, as one reviewer notes, registering Codex project trust for the wrong directory.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:156-174 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `upsert` performs an unguarded list-then-create-or-PATCH operation.
  WHY: Concurrent runs can create duplicate tracker issues or overwrite entries written by another run.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:185-212 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: A fix issue is created before the verdict comment, but the fix issue is not deduplicated by source if posting the verdict comment fails.
  WHY: A retry without the verdict marker can create another fix issue for the same source.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:185-201, 210-211; scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:576-578 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: Failed code-gap or operator-step writes only emit warnings, while the verdict marker can still be posted and treated as final.
  WHY: Later project checks skip on the marker, so missing work is not retried; if issue creation succeeds but verdict posting fails, a retry can create a duplicate issue.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:192 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Model-generated fix text can contain control characters that are not removed before the fix-issue request.
  WHY: The GitHub API request can fail while the script continues and posts a verdict that reports code gaps without creating the fix issue.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:129-132 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The changed-file list uses `MERGE_SHA^1..MERGE_SHA` and silently caps the result at 200 paths.
  WHY: The list can omit earlier commits in a rebase-and-merge PR and paths beyond the cap, leaving activation verification with incomplete context.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:129-132 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Failure of the changed-file `git diff` command is suppressed and can produce an empty changed-file list without a diagnostic.
  WHY: Verification then proceeds with no file-level context and no warning.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml:20 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The issue-open clarify predicate does not exclude `ai:operator-step`.
  WHY: The human-steps tracker can enter the automated clarify and implementation pipeline; severity disagreement: one reviewer rated this MAJOR, while the others rated it BLOCKER.
- .github/workflows/internal-clarify.yml:18 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The internal clarify predicate does not exclude `ai:operator-step`.
  WHY: The operator-step tracker can enter the automated clarify and implementation pipeline.
- workflow-templates/ai-clarify.yml:17-20 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The consumer-facing clarify predicate does not exclude `ai:operator-step`.
  WHY: Consumer repositories can route human-only operator steps into their automated clarify and implementation pipeline.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:173 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: Issue creation sends `labels[]` as a form field instead of sending a `labels` array.
  WHY: The issue may be created without the `ai:operator-step` label, so later label-filtered lookups cannot find it and can create further unlabelled issues.
- README.md:61 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` secrets-table row omits `issue_pr_status` from the workflows using the secret.
  WHY: Operators following the documentation may omit the secret from that workflow, causing activation verification to fail in consumer repositories.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:76-85 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: Verdict normalization discards gaps after the first 20.
  WHY: Later gaps are omitted from the verdict and from code-fix and operator-step handling despite the prompt requiring every gap to be acted on.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:121, 192, 210 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The linked-issue read, fix-issue creation, and verdict-comment post use raw `gh api` calls without retries.
  WHY: Transient API failures can silently lose a read or write and prevent the associated verification work from being completed.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:567-606 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `run_project_activation_verify` has no lock around the already-verified check and worktree lifecycle.
  WHY: Concurrent poll ticks can race to create or remove the same worktree, and a failed worktree add is treated as a skip.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:100-107 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Early-return guards can silently skip activation when required environment or job context is missing without identifying the underlying missing setup.
  WHY: Operators may see only a generic skip reason and cannot distinguish a missing worktree, repository, or PR context.
- .github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml:11-12 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Consumers with explicit secret mappings that omit the new optional `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` input will run activation verification without that key.
  WHY: Those consumers can silently skip activation verification when the Codex call cannot authenticate.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:174-176 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The read-only Codex call receives PR and linked-issue text and can read files from the merged code without an instruction to ignore potentially sensitive repository content.
  WHY: Read-only sandboxing prevents writes but does not prevent reading repository files.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: “Steps only a person can take; the pipeline continues and the gated work stays off until they are done.” Issues carrying `ai:operator-step` must not enter the AI clarification pipeline.
  expected_change_site: `.github/workflows/clarify.yml`, `.github/workflows/internal-clarify.yml`, `workflow-templates/ai-clarify.yml`, and `tests/test_phase_wrapper_predicate_contract.py`
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: All three clarify workflow predicates exclude other tracker labels but not `ai:operator-step`; the predicate contract test does not assert the exclusion.
- requirement: The PR description claims “812 passed with no failures” and “Phase 7 sweep ... 3504 passed.”
  expected_change_site: CI pipeline `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` job and the PR head commit
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: The check-run context reports `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` failed with `5 failed, 171 passed` on head SHA `4903f590c14691bd2e157b507ede984d75ece8d2`; the failure log identifies merge-guard hook tests.
- requirement: Activation verification in project mode must be verified end-to-end for completed orchestrator projects.
  expected_change_site: `tests/test_activation_verify.py`
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  EVIDENCE: `tests/test_activation_verify.py` tests only `pr` mode and has no project-mode invocation or test of `run_project_activation_verify` environment propagation.
- requirement: `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` must be updated in lockstep with `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` to support `NAME+=` assignment prefixes.
  expected_change_site: `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: The source hook does not support `+=`, while the template does; the reported tests include `test_template_copies_are_identical` and parameterized guard tests for `COUNT+=1 git push`.

=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:87 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_trusted` trusts any GitHub login ending in `[bot]`, allowing an external bot's issue to be selected as the operator-step tracker.
  WHY: `upsert` can write operator steps into an attacker-controlled issue.
- scripts/orchestrat
